title: Three-view markerless 3D hand-motion protocol
author: Hideto Tobishima
materials: Start recording on all three cameras.
Mark the hand start position with tape.
Temporal synchronization across cameras Script: time_sync.py
Sum squared inter-ray distances across landmarks and frames.
3D reconstruction with dual-route output Script: data_integration.py
Database construction for reliability analysis Script: database.py

steps.title: Configure Camera Setup
steps.instruction: Set up a three-camera system to record reach-and-grasp movements on a tabletop.

substeps.instruction: Place Camera A frontal to the participant, aligned with the midsagittal plane on the opposite side of the table, framing the full tabletop.
Place Camera B at the left-anterior oblique position, approximately 45 degrees from the frontal view.
Place Camera C at the right-anterior oblique position, approximately 45 degrees from the frontal view.
Set all cameras to a height of approximately 120 cm and approximately 80 cm from the center of the tabletop measurement volume.
Configure all cameras to 1920 x 1080 resolution and 30 fps.
Disable auto-exposure and autofocus if manual control is available.

steps.title: Verify Tracking and Adjust Angles
steps.instruction: Ensure hand landmarks are trackable across all views during a practice task.

substeps.instruction: Ask the participant to perform a practice reach-and-grasp task.
Use a real-time landmark overlay to confirm all 21 hand landmarks remain trackable in all three views.
Adjust camera angles until the hand is visible from at least two cameras during object contact and lift, ensuring the table, start position, object position, and movement path are framed.

steps.title: Calibrate Camera Volume
steps.instruction: Perform stereo calibration using a checkerboard to determine camera parameters.

substeps.instruction: Move a checkerboard (22 mm squares, 10 x 7 inner corners) through the measurement volume for at least 30 seconds, varying orientation and depth while remaining visible in all three cameras.
Stop recording and transfer calibration videos to the analysis workstation.
Run the calibration script to estimate intrinsic parameters for each camera via checkerboard detection.
Estimate pairwise extrinsic parameters between Camera A-B and Camera A-C using stereo calibration with fixed intrinsics.
Save intrinsics, distortion coefficients, extrinsics, and inter-camera baseline to a calibration.npz file.

steps.title: Prepare Participant and Environment
steps.instruction: Position the participant and target object for the recording session.

substeps.instruction: Seat the participant without shoes at the edge of a 45 cm chair in upright unsupported sitting.
Place the table anterior to the participant at 70 cm height.
Set the start upper-limb posture: shoulder neutral, elbow flexed to 90 degrees, forearm pronated, and hand resting on the tabletop.
Place the target object on the participant midline, 30 cm anterior to the start position.
Mark the object and hand start positions with tape for consistency across conditions.

steps.title: Record Reach-and-Grasp Trials
steps.instruction: Capture synchronized video of the hand movements across different conditions.

substeps.instruction: Start all three cameras on a single verbal cue.
Instruct the participant to reach forward from the start posture, grasp the target object, lift it, return it to the marked position, and return the hand to the start position.
Record three consecutive reach-grasp-return cycles as one set.
Record two sets per object condition (bottle and ball) for both affected and unaffected sides.
Stop cameras on a verbal cue after the third cycle of the final set.
Save videos with a naming convention including participant ID, side, object condition, set number, and camera ID (e.g., 01_Paretic_bottle_set1_CamA.MOV).

steps.title: Extract 2D Landmarks
steps.instruction: Process recorded videos to extract hand landmark coordinates.

substeps.instruction: Load each camera video in Python and process frame-by-frame using MediaPipe Hands.
Extract 2D pixel coordinates and visibility values for the 21 hand landmarks.
Read frame time using OpenCV CAP_PROP_POS_MSEC.
Save per-camera CSV files containing frame index, timestamp (seconds), 2D x and y coordinates, and visibility for all 21 landmarks.

steps.title: Synchronize Camera Data
steps.instruction: Determine and apply temporal offsets between the three camera streams.

substeps.instruction: Load the three 2D landmark CSV files and calibration.npz.

For candidate temporal offsets within a prespecified search window, perform provisional triangulation by back-projecting camera rays and computing the minimum inter-ray distance for each landmark and frame.
Select the offset that minimizes total squared inter-ray distance.
Output SYNC_TIME_A, SYNC_TIME_B, and SYNC_TIME_C values to the console for use in data_integration.py.
Apply synchronization offsets and resample 2D data to a uniform 30 fps grid using linear interpolation.

steps.title: Reconstruct 3D Coordinates
steps.instruction: Perform 3D reconstruction using a hierarchical DLT triangulation approach.

substeps.instruction: Compute primary three-camera (ABC) and fallback two-camera (AB, AC, BC) 3D reconstructions using DLT triangulation for every frame and landmark.
Evaluate candidates by mean reprojection error across available views.

Screen candidates based on two constraints: index-finger proximal-phalanx length between 10.0 mm and 80.0 mm, and mean reprojection error below 10.0 mm (using a pixel-to-mm conversion based on a working-distance estimate of 2.0 x Camera A-B baseline).
Require that the index-finger metacarpophalangeal joint (landmark 5) is detected by all contributing cameras to evaluate the anatomical constraint.
Adopt the ABC candidate if it satisfies both constraints; otherwise, fall back to the two-camera combination with the lowest reprojection error that satisfies the constraints.

Classify frames failing all constraints as 'rescue frames'. In the 'Raw' dataset, retain the coordinate from the combination with the lowest reprojection error; in the 'Strict' dataset, set these frames to NaN.

steps.title: Filter and Export Data
steps.instruction: Generate filtered and unfiltered datasets for validation and analysis.

substeps.instruction: Compute the valid-frame rate (accepted frames / total frames) per landmark and save as Valid_Frame_Rate.csv.
Output Route A: Unfiltered_Raw.csv and Unfiltered_Strict.csv (no temporal filtering).
Output Route B: Raw.csv and Strict.csv after applying a fourth-order zero-lag Butterworth low-pass filter at 6.0 Hz.
Preserve NaN values in the Strict dataset during filtering; do not interpolate rescue frames before filtering.

steps.title: Validate Reconstruction Accuracy
steps.instruction: Analyze reprojection errors to validate the 3D reconstruction.

substeps.instruction: Load Unfiltered_Raw.csv and calibration.npz.
Project 3D points back to camera image planes and compute the Euclidean pixel error against original MediaPipe 2D coordinates.
Convert pixel error to millimeters using a scaling factor derived from intrinsics and the average 3D Z coordinates of the wrist, index-finger MCP, and middle-finger MCP.
Report mean and maximum reprojection error for each landmark in pixels and millimeters.
Perform sensitivity analysis by varying the working-distance values by -30% to +30% (0.70, 0.85, 1.00, 1.15, and 1.30 x nominal) and report resulting bounds.

steps.title: Evaluate Anatomical Stability
steps.instruction: Compare the stability of 3D reconstruction against monocular tracking.

substeps.instruction: Load Unfiltered_Raw.csv and Unfiltered_Strict.csv.
Apply a fourth-order zero-lag 2.0 Hz Butterworth low-pass filter (preserving NaNs in Strict).
Compute 3D Euclidean distance for 14 anatomical segment pairs.
Calculate mean length, standard deviation (SD), and coefficient of variation (CV = SD/mean) for each segment.
Report the mean CV across all 14 segments as the global anatomical stability index.
Repeat the process using only Camera A data (monocular input) and compare its 14-segment mean CV to the three-camera Strict dataset to determine the gain in stability.

steps.title: Analyze Reliability and Error
steps.instruction: Compute ICC and measurement error for the 14 anatomical segments.

substeps.instruction: Load Trial 1 and Trial 2 from the 6.0 Hz filtered Strict dataset (Route B) for each participant and condition.
Compute per-frame lengths for the 14 anatomical segment pairs and calculate the trial-wise temporal mean length (excluding NaNs).
Save results to ICC_Database_14Pairs.csv, ensuring canonical Title-case condition labels to avoid duplicates.
Using the icc.py script, compute the two-way random-effects, absolute-agreement, single-measurement intraclass correlation coefficient, ICC (2,1), using pingouin.
Compute Standard Error of Measurement: SEM = SD * sqrt(1 - ICC).
Compute Minimal Detectable Change at 95% confidence: MDC95 = 1.96 * sqrt(2) * SEM.
Report ICC (2,1), 95% CI, SEM, and MDC95 for all 14 segments.
